title: Antiderivatives & the Definite Integral
summary: An antiderivative reverses differentiation; the indefinite integral $\int f\,dx$ collects them all (plus $+C$). The definite integral $\int_a^b f\,dx$ is a limit of Riemann sums measuring net area, and the Fundamental Theorem ties the two together.

antiderivative.plain: A function whose derivative is the given one.

Riemann sum.plain: Adding up rectangle areas to approximate area under a curve.
Riemann sum.in_class: $\sum f(x_i)\Delta x$; the integral is its limit.

definite integral.plain: Net signed area between the curve and the axis on $[a,b]$.

net area.plain: Area above the axis minus area below.
net area.in_class: Regions under the axis count negative.

concept_sections.heading: Antiderivatives
concept_sections.explanation: To undo a derivative, raise the power and divide: $\int x^n\,dx=\dfrac{x^{n+1}}{n+1}+C$. Every antiderivative differs by a constant, hence the $+C$.

concept_sections.heading: Basic integral formulas
concept_sections.explanation: Reverse the standard derivatives: $\int\cos x\,dx=\sin x+C$, $\int e^x\,dx=e^x+C$, $\int\frac1x\,dx=\ln|x|+C$.
math_steps: Recall the derivative that produces the integrand.

concept_sections.heading: Riemann sums and area
concept_sections.explanation: Slice $[a,b]$ into rectangles of width $\Delta x$, sum their areas $\sum f(x_i)\Delta x$, and let $\Delta x\to0$. The limit is the definite integral — the (net) area under the curve.

concept_sections.heading: The Fundamental Theorem
concept_sections.explanation: To evaluate $\int_a^b f\,dx$, find any antiderivative $F$ and compute $F(b)-F(a)$. This converts area (a limit of sums) into a single subtraction.
math_steps: That number is the definite integral.

concept_sections.heading: Net vs total area
concept_sections.explanation: The definite integral counts area below the axis as negative. For total (unsigned) area, split at the roots and integrate the absolute value piecewise.
math_steps: Add magnitudes for total area, or keep signs for net area.

real_world_examples.title: Distance from velocity
real_world_examples.scenario: A car's velocity is recorded over time.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The definite integral of velocity is the net displacement — the Fundamental Theorem in action.

real_world_examples.title: Total rainfall
real_world_examples.scenario: A gauge reports rainfall rate through a storm.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Integrating the rate over the storm's duration gives total accumulated rainfall.

real_world_examples.title: Area of an odd region
real_world_examples.scenario: Land bounded by a curved river.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: A definite integral computes the area under the boundary curve.
